subject: SLA: monthly credit smoothing & uptime baseline
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena@datavanta.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@datavanta.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: SLA request: monthly credit smoothing & uptime baseline

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — DataVanta liked the latency profile and the multi-tenant routing options. We are now working through procurement and have a couple of asks on the SLA template before we can sign.

High level:
- We need an initial uptime baseline of 99.8% for the first 90 days after go-live (we can target 99.9% thereafter). This is to account for our heavy traffic ramp and planned phased rollouts across regions.
- We'd like the monthly service credit to be "smoothed" across two billing cycles rather than applied fully to the invoice for the month of the incident (so Credits Month N can be used against Month N and N+1).
- A cap on total credits is important for us; we propose a cap equal to 150% of the monthly invoice rather than Redwood's standard 100% cap.

We've attached our proposed redline for the SLA (DataVanta_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf) to show how we'd word the temporary baseline and smoothing. Are these changes something Redwood would consider, or should we go through a formal amendment process?

Appreciate the swift reply — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Lena Park
Head of Infrastructure
DataVanta
[lena@datavanta.io]

Subject: Re: SLA request: monthly credit smoothing & uptime baseline

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear note and for flagging the redline. Glad DataVanta is seeing the value.

Quick responses to your asks:
- Redwood's standard availability baseline for hosted customers is 99.9% (monthly). We can consider a temporary ramp for the first 60–90 days, but we need explicit monitoring/ops checkpoints to avoid open-ended exceptions.
- Smoothing credits across two billing cycles is something our finance team can support operationally; we typically apply credits to the month of occurrence, but we can add language to allow application across the incident month + following month.
- On cap: Redwood's default cap is 100% of the monthly invoice. Moving to 150% materially increases vendor exposure. Ben and I discussed; as a compromise we could accept a 150% cap limited to a single 90-day onboarding window and only for usage-billed invoices (not committed reserved capacity).

I've attached our suggested SLA amendment (Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v2.docx) with a proposed phased uplift: 99.8% for month 0–2, 99.9% thereafter, smoothing language, and a 150% cap limited to the 90-day window. I'll loop Legal in to get a redline back to you.

Proposed next step: review Marissa's comments and, if acceptable, we can prepare a short amendment and move to DocuSign.

Best,

Subject: RE: SLA request: monthly credit smoothing & uptime baseline (internal)

Grace / Ben — quick legal read of Lena's asks and Grace's proposed compromise. Key points:

1) Temporary phased uplift: rather than open-ended 90 days, we should define a 3-step phased schedule that automatically sunsets unless DataVanta requests an extension in writing. Suggested language: 99.8% for first 30 days post-activation, 99.85% for days 31–60, 99.9% thereafter (this gives us a measured ramp that aligns with monitoring windows).
2) Cap: 150% for the onboarding window only, but limit applicability to variable usage charges (exclude committed reserved capacity and third-party pass-throughs). Add a carve-out for incidents caused by customer configuration or scheduled maintenance.
3) Smoothing: allow credits to be applied across incident month + next billing month, but require the customer to notify finance within 30 days to elect smoothing. This prevents indefinite credit liabilities.
4) Monitoring & ops: require weekly ops sync for the first 60 days with a short escalation path (ops_oncall@redwood.com) and shareable dashboards.

I'll produce a marked-up redline (Redline_Notes_Marissa_v1.pdf) and recommend we send it to Lena with a cover note proposing the phased schedule above. If DataVanta pushes back on the phase steps, we can fall back to your 90-day single-step suggestion.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: SLA request: monthly credit smoothing & uptime baseline

Thanks Grace and Marissa — appreciate the thoughtful counterproposals. We're aligned on the goal here. A few clarifications from our procurement/legal team:

- The phased approach is fine, but DataVanta would prefer the uplift schedule to be a 90-day window with two steps for operational simplicity: 99.8% for days 0–44 and 99.9% from day 45 onward. That gives our rollout teams a full six-week buffer.
- On the cap: we can accept Redwood's carve-outs for reserved capacity and customer-caused incidents, but procurement is firm on a 150% cap for the onboarding window. If you need a guardrail, we can accept a cap of 150% limited to the first 90 days only.
- Smoothing election: fine with the 30-day election requirement; procurement prefers the election be automatic unless the customer opts out on the first notice.

If we can get those points captured in a single-page amendment, procurement will route to our CFO for signature next week. Please send your final redline and the DocuSign package.

Best,
Lena Park
Head of Infrastructure
DataVanta

Hi Lena / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. We discussed internally and can accept the compromise in the following final form:

Summary of agreed terms (for amendment):
- Phased onboarding baseline: 99.8% for days 0–44 post-activation; 99.9% from day 45 onward (per DataVanta preference).
- Service credit smoothing: credits for an incident may be applied to the invoice for the month of the incident and the following month. Customer may opt out; otherwise smoothing is automatic if finance is not notified within 30 days.
- Cap: 150% of the monthly invoice for the specified onboarding window only (first 90 days). Cap excludes committed reserved capacity and incidents caused by customer configuration or third-party services.
- Ops: weekly operational syncs for the first 60 days and access to shared availability dashboards.

Next steps:
1) Attached is the single-page amendment (SLA_Amendment_Final_DocuSign.docx). Please confirm and we'll send the DocuSign link to your CFO.
2) Ben will coordinate the billing treatment for smoothing so your finance team has a clear credit ledger.
3) Marissa will attach the final legal exhibit and countersign in DocuSign.

I'll kick off the DocuSign envelope once you confirm. Thanks for working through this quickly — looking forward to go-live.
